Small Steps, Big Change

Our planet is facing serious problems, such as pollution and climate change. However, students can play an important part in protecting it.

First of all, we can reduce the waste we produce. Instead of buying plastic bottles every day, we can use a reusable bottle. We can also recycle paper and use both sides of our notebooks. Secondly, saving water and energy is easy. Turning off the tap while we brush our teeth and switching off the lights when we leave a room will save a lot over a year.

In addition, we can take part in school activities such as planting trees and cleaning the streets near our school.

In conclusion, protecting the environment is not only the job of governments. If every student makes a small effort, our future will be much greener.

Finally, a trip to a museum with friends or family is a pleasant and cheap way to spend a day.

I strongly advise every student to visit at least one museum this year. You will return home with new ideas and a better understanding of your country.

First, think about what you enjoy and what you are good at. A student who loves solving problems may succeed in engineering, while one who enjoys helping others may prefer medicine or teaching.

Finally, do not choose a subject only because your friends have chosen it or because it sounds impressive. What suits them may not suit you.

In conclusion, a wise choice is based on interests, skills and good information. If you follow this advice, you will be more likely to enjoy your studies and your career.

items.title: Why everyone should learn first aid

points: Why it is useful at home and school
items.model:
Be Ready to Help

Accidents can happen at any time, so everyone should know basic first aid.

First aid means the simple help that we give to an injured person until a doctor arrives. For example, we can clean a small cut, stop a nosebleed or call an ambulance quickly. These actions can prevent a small problem from becoming a serious one.

First aid is useful at home, at school and on the street. A child may fall in the playground, or an elderly person may feel dizzy. If a trained student is nearby, he can help immediately and stay calm.

Students can learn first aid by attending school courses, joining the Red Crescent or watching reliable videos with an adult.

In conclusion, learning first aid takes only a few hours, but it may save a life. I urge all my classmates to learn it.

Smartphones: Use Them Wisely

Smartphones are everywhere, and most teenagers cannot imagine a day without them. Are they a blessing or a curse?

On the one hand, a smartphone is a useful tool. We can search for information, use a dictionary, call our family and learn languages with free apps. It also keeps us connected with friends. A phone can also be an alarm clock, a camera and a map in one small device, which is why so many people depend on it.

On the other hand, using a phone too much can cause problems. Many students waste hours on games and social media, so they sleep late and study less. Some of them even forget how to talk to people face to face.

My advice is simple. Set a time limit every day, turn off notifications while you study and spend time with your family.

In conclusion, a smartphone is a good servant but a bad master. The choice is ours.

items.title: Protecting the sea

items.model:
Save Our Seas

The sea gives us food, work and enjoyment, but today it is in danger.

The main cause of sea pollution is rubbish, especially plastic. Ships also leave oil in the water, and some factories send their waste into it. As a result, fish and turtles die when they swallow plastic, and the beaches become dirty.

People suffer, too. When the sea is polluted, there are fewer fish, so fishermen earn less money, and tourists stay away. Many families also lose an important place for rest and play, because nobody wants to swim in dirty water.

However, we can help. We should never throw rubbish on the beach, we should use bags that can be used again, and we should join clean-up campaigns. Governments must also punish those who pollute the sea.

In conclusion, the sea is a gift, and we must protect it for future generations before it is too late.

Succeeding in Your Exams

The final year of school is difficult, but with the right habits every student can succeed.

First, plan your time. Make a weekly timetable and give more time to the subjects that you find hard. Study in short periods of forty minutes with short breaks, and revise regularly instead of waiting until the last week.

Second, look after your health. Sleeping well, eating healthy meals and walking every day will keep your mind clear. Staying awake all night before an exam usually does more harm than good. A short walk after studying can help you to remember what you have learned and give you more energy for the next lesson.

Finally, stay positive. Everyone feels worried sometimes, but believing in yourself helps you to concentrate. Talk to your teachers or family if you feel stressed.

In conclusion, success does not come by luck. It comes from planning, health and confidence.

Friends in the Digital Age

Technology has changed the way we make and keep friends.

First, it has made communication easier. Today we can send a message to a friend in another country in a second, share photos and play games together. As a result, friends who live far away can stay close.

In my opinion, technology is useful only when it supports real friendship and does not replace it. We should meet our friends regularly, speak kindly and be careful online.

In short, the best friendships still need time, honesty and care.

Travelling Abroad: First-Time Tips

Travelling to another country for the first time is exciting, but it needs careful planning.

Before the journey, check that your passport is valid and prepare a list of what to pack. Do not forget to keep copies of important papers and to tell your family your plans. It is also wise to pack a small bag with a charger, a bottle of water and a snack in case of a long wait.

During the journey, arrive at the airport early and keep your passport and ticket in a safe place. If you feel nervous, ask a member of the crew, because they are always happy to help.

In the new country, respect local customs and be polite with everyone. Learn a few useful words in the local language and keep in touch with your family.

In conclusion, good preparation and a friendly attitude will make your trip safe and enjoyable.

Welcoming Guests: A Tradition to Keep

Hospitality has always been an important part of our culture. It means welcoming guests with kindness and generosity and making them feel at home.

It is important for several reasons. First, it strengthens the relationships between families, neighbours and friends. Second, it teaches us to think about the feelings of other people. Third, it makes our society warmer and more united. When people feel welcome, they trust each other more, and small quarrels become easier to solve.

Young people can practise hospitality in simple ways. They can greet guests with a smile, offer them a drink and listen politely to what they say. They can also welcome a new student at school and show him around.

In conclusion, hospitality is a value that we should be proud of. We must keep it alive by practising it every day, at home and outside.
